chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid, from Abu Al-Rabie who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is your view regarding bartering dates and unripened red dates, a similar portion with a similar portion?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'So (what about) the cooked juice and the juice, similar with similar?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.التَّمْر: Dates (the fruit of the date palm)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.مِثْلًا بِمِثْلٍ: Like for like / equal quantity of the same kind

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging dates for unripened dates or juice for juice in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the application of *mithlan bi-mithl* (equal for equal) in *Riba al-Fadl* specifically for date varieties and their processed forms, establishing that unripened red dates and cooked juice are treated as the same species as their fresh counterparts. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition of excess in barter applies to the specific commodity type rather than just its raw state, ensuring fairness in daily commercial transactions.
